newsitem.title: FINLAND: FISKARS CEO SEES "GOOD" Q3 REPORT.
newsitem.headline: FISKARS CEO SEES "GOOD" Q3 REPORT.

text.p: Finnish durable consumer goods group Fiskars Oy Ab's third quarter report will be good, Fiskars' CEO Stig Stendahl said on Friday.
Stendahl told Reuters in an interview that overall sales in the group were on track.
"We had a good first-half report, and I don't see any reason why we would not have a good report also for the third quarter. Our net sales have developed fairly well," he said.
Fiskars' January-September interim report is due to be released on November 20.
The group's January-June profit before extraordinary items was 139 million markka, up from 122 million, and above the highest forecast in a Reuters poll -- 128 million markka.
Its first-half net sales fell to 1.10 billion markka from 1.21 billion.
Lower-than-expected weak sales of garden scissors which Finnish News Agency STT on Thursday said would lead to lay-offs at Fiskars' Billnas factory will have no impact on its earnings, Stendahl said.
Demand for garden scissors was dampened by poor weather conditions last spring in the U.S., he said.
"There is no drama. I would say demand has been lower than we hoped," he said.
The Billnas plant accounted for about seven percent of Fiskars' 2.3 billion markka net sales in 1995, he said.
